notes:
Lead: growth-stage notifications platform for ecom merchants. Primary pain: nightly traffic spikes when cart reminders and price-drop pushes fire off — they see short windows with high concurrency and occasional 429 responses from our hosted endpoints.

They are SMB (51-200) but cost-sensitive; want to stay on hosted API (no private deployment). Key asks: clear quota semantics, per-api-key rate limits, per-route concurrency caps, predictable burst behavior (how long/size of burst allowed), guidance for client-side backoff and retry windows, and an example SDK implementation.

Customer quote: "We need graceful degradation — a few 429s are OK if UX shows queued state and retries are smooth. But sudden 429 spikes during promos have caused cart abandonment."

Technical details shared by customer: typical baseline 20-30 req/s, spikes to 200 req/s for 30-90s during promos. Many requests are short-chat completions (streaming not used yet). They prefer token-cost visibility but want per-route concurrency isolation so the notifications route can’t starve the support-chat route.

Recommended internal play: propose a hosted plan with burst window + throttling thresholds, point to Optimize hints (batching + prefix cache), and provide sample backoff snippet. Attach pricing round and one-page SLA note.
